utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed, Mr. Traldi, that you would want to raise a preliminary matter. Is it a very short one so that the witness can be escorted into the courtroom or would we need a bit more time?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think it might take a minute or two, Your Honour, and I would request that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cvoro.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before Mr. Traldi continues, I would like to remind you again that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We left off yesterday discussing the assistance you provided in establishing SRNA. Turning now to some other Bosnian Serb institutions, the municipal government of Pale was also supposed to supply organs of the Republika Srpska in Pale with accommodation; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The municipal government in Pale was supposed to supply organs of the Republika Srpska with telephone lines?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Telephone numbers that were not indispensable were mobilised, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, such cases also happened. Those that were indispensable to the functioning of the authorities at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask about just a couple of examples. Telephone numbers were mobilised for the government; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only for the government, also for all the other institutions that moved to Pale. The capacity of the post office at Pale was very small. It wasn't enough even for all the citizens of Pale and their needs before the war. A large number of citizens --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- did not have telephone sets --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I could --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I just wanted to explain what the situation had been before --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any need to explain, Mr. Traldi will ask for it, and at the end of the matter we have discussed, if you think that there is something that really needs to be further explained, you can briefly hint at that and then most likely you will be allowed to give an explanation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To return to the couple of examples that I was going to ask you about, phone numbers were mobilised for the Bosnian Serb Presidency; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And other numbers were mobilised for the Bosnian Serb Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For all the institutions, as I've said, beginning with Presidency, the Assembly, and all the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi will phrase his question. If he wants to go one by one, you should follow as a witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which other Bosnian Serb institutions did you intend to refer to a moment ago for which telephone numbers were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the needs of the army, for the needs of the radio, the television, all the ministries that made up the government, the military hospital, they needed the greatest number of telephone numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, turning now to your role as president of the Executive Board in Pale municipality, the Executive Board was affiliated with the Municipal Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Assembly is the largest law-making branch of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Executive Board was involved as a result with the municipal budget, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, the Executive Board made the proposal and the budget was approved by the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd like to look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. You said -- no, I got it. I think I misunderstood something, but re-reading the question and answer makes it unnecessary to put any further question. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to look at one example of a budget proposal. If we could have 65 ter 30711.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, first, here on page 1 in both languages, do you recognise your name towards the bottom right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the top left we see this document comes from the Executive Board; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What we see here is a decision on the budget of the Pale municipality for May 1992, and under Article 2 we see a list of expenditures made; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And among others, we see fuel expenditures for the Crisis Staff, the Executive Board, and the TO; correct? And it's under point 1: "Organi uprave"?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are several entities, they are enumerated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning now to page 3 in the English but still on page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a list of other users and we see what looks like 100.000 dinars --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see in the Serbian. I only see the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist if --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if the witness only sees the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I see it. The assets of the Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's exactly what I was going to direct your attention to, sir. What appears to be funding to the Serb Democratic Party in Pale; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see how it rates compared to other items. Those are minor funds and they were meant to finance the Serb Democratic Party, to cover -- to cover costs for the previous month and the funds were raised in the previous month --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- however, generally the law on budget --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Actually, I think you might have been about to say what I'm about to ask you which is: The budget generally provided for funds for political parties, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For all the political parties that formed the government, that participated in governing, received funds from the budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the SDS is the only political party funded in this document; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that party had absolute power at Pale, and at that time and until I don't know for how long exactly, they operated from Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 30711.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30711 receives number P6562, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6562 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just have one question. Mr. Cvoro, were there any other parties other than the SDS in the Pale Assembly, Municipal Assembly of Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The SDA participated in the government, SDS, and SDP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And may I ask a follow-up question. Did the other two parties also receive funding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time they were not active, they were not working, they didn't need financing. This is the budget only for the month of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the following month, did the other parties receive any funding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the next month we didn't have a budget because the war broke out and we moved to humanitarian aid and the distribution of basic necessities. This was just a temporary request to the budget for financing the government by the budget. The municipality of Pale was part of the city. All the funds that we distributed from taxes, contributions, and communal taxes and fees went to the account of the city and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- city distributed assets according to a certain key.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm only interested if only the SDS was financed by the municipal budget or if at any point in time also the other parties received money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the regular budget, funds were also planned for the financing of other parties, all the parties that participated in government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And did they receive the money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe they did. I cannot say now yes or no, but the funds for them were allocated and they probably received them. What I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, you have answered --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- explain is that we get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have answered my question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, turning to another position you held now. You mentioned Friday that you also served as president of the Pale Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's not mentioned in your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The crisis --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement contains an explanation of my understanding of the role of Crisis Staffs. I'm not sure, but I think it's there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But an explanation of the role, is that the same as you serving on that Crisis Staff as president? I can explain the position of the Belgian government, but that doesn't make me a member of the Belgian government, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say that I was president of the Crisis Staff for a short period of time, and that can be seen from the documents that I signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it's not in your statement; that was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember now the exact text of that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Crisis Staff operated for about two months; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For approximately two months, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And specifically that would be approximately April and May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When your Crisis Staff had material needs, it would request assistance from the Bosnian Serb authorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd just like to look at two quick examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 03662 brought to our screens, and I'd ask for page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So looking at the centre, lower part of the page in the original, do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we can see this is from the Pale Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is a request for material assistance for the normal functioning of the administration organs and municipality organs of Pale; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The request includes writing machines; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And various office material?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Telephones?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I won't go through each example.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But if we could turn back to page 1 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here we have a letter from Mr. Djeric, and looking at the first paragraph he writes: "In the addition to this document, we are joining the specification of the needs of Pale municipality for making this area as equipped as possible in order to correspond to the newly created conditions." So the government of the Serbian Republic of BiH is supporting your request for supplies here; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it here. Although I see it for the first time, it's obviously a document of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 03662.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03662 receives number P6563, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6563 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd ask for 65 ter 03693.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, in the document we looked at a second ago, in the request where writing machines, et cetera, are asked, it is also explained that one of the reasons is that they had given away all their equipment and material to the government and the republic organs, so that it's rather refunding for what was paid for by themselves. Is that something you want to draw our attention to as well or -- because --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's something, Mr. President, that I thought was evident from the document, but I agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- certainly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- yes, all the other, that writing machines are there, is just as self-evident from the document as this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's true, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This document, similarly, reads: "The Pale Municipality Crisis Staff addressed the Government of the Serbian Republic of BiH with the request to help them procure the fuel necessary for transport of refugees ..." And then in the next paragraph says: "Considering the above, we kindly ask you to deliver one cistern of fuel to DD 'Romanijaprevoz' from Pale, as soon as possible, to be used for the designated purpose of transporting refugees. "The pro forma invoice for the delivered fuel shall be submitted to the Budget of the Serbian Republic of BiH." And in the bottom corner we see the signature of Mr. Djeric again. This document, sir, also shows the government of the RS responding to your Crisis Staff's requests and supporting them; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does assist them, and our capacities were not enough for all the requirements of sending refugees. I said already there were five to ten buses daily filled with refugees going to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 03693.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03693 receives number P6564, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6564 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, your evidence in your statement is that Crisis Staffs were set up pursuant to binding orders from the Presidency of the SFRY; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in keeping with the law and the instructions of the SFRY Presidency and the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received considerable evidence that Bosnian Serb authorities also issued instructions to form Serb Crisis Staffs. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any specific cases. I know that Crisis Staffs were automatically established in keeping with the law in the entire territory of Republika Srpska and I believe in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, when you say "in keeping with the law," you're a professor of All People's Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I professionally oversaw contingency plans and defence plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the word "Crisis Staffs," it's not explicitly used in the ONO law, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the law, but in the instructions of the Presidency of the SFRY and BH, yes, there are Crisis Staffs because they are in charge of plans for emergency situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd just look at a similar set of instructions, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P3038. These are the Variant A and B instructions. And if we could have page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd direct your attention to point 3, which notes: "SDS municipal boards shall establish immediately Crisis Staffs of the Serbian People in the municipality ..." And then it lists the people who shall be members. Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly. I mean, you've probably read it correctly, but I've never seen these instructions and I never had them before me. They asked me about that when I testified for Mr. Radovan Karadzic, I said the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So my question for you was simply: Did I read that correctly? And can I take it your answer was: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that. I don't know what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't -- you just have to listen to the question. Did Mr. Traldi read correctly what is in this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll read again to permit you to answer it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Traldi, even if the witness would say you did not read correctly, the Chamber is in a position to verify whether you read it correctly or not. So if the witness has any problems -- we followed Mr. Traldi's words and he read it, at least this portion, correctly, Mr. Cvoro. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm relieved to hear that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this document shows that the Bosnian Serb authorities also issued instructions to form Crisis Staffs; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, yes, but I've never received any such instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, in paragraph 12 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm done with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before it goes, earlier you indicated, Mr. Cvoro, that there were other parties in the Pale Municipal Assembly. I see this instruction at paragraph 3 refers only to the SDS. Are other parties not -- were they not part of the Crisis Staff that had to be established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. I'm telling you -- I mean, these instructions, over here, the last paragraph 3, says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot find the reference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, if that means something, I've read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You didn't answer my question. My question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- but the interpreters said that they could not find what you read, the last paragraph 3. Could you please read that again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is paragraph 3 of these instructions that have been presented to me and it's the last paragraph of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that where it says: "The Commander shall appoint a member of the ..." Is that the part you had on your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll read it for you. "The Commander shall appoint a member of the Crisis Staff to be the Co-ordinator for Relations with the SDA ... municipal leaders." You wanted to draw our attention to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see that that is written there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you a few questions on the matter. Your Crisis Staff in Pale, was that composed exclusively of Serb members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only Serb members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the SDA consulted before you established that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not a political person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not what --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was a non-political person. I mean -- no, I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know. You said the Crisis Staff which you presided over for a short period was in accordance with the law and regulations. You explained to us that the word "Crisis Staff" does not appear in the law. Does the Crisis Staff appear in the regulations in the sense that Crisis Staff of exclusively one ethnicity can be established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. I don't know. I'm not aware of any of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since your Crisis Staff was exclusively composed of Serb members, would you agree with me that there could be at least a discussion about whether such a Crisis Staff would be in line with the existing legislation and regulations, it being exclusively Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, members of the Crisis Staff were the leaders of the executive organs, the representatives of political organisations, and representatives of the members of parliament who were in the Assembly. Now, why there wasn't a member of the SDA or some other party, I don't know. That was decided upon by the political echelons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, is that a "yes" to my question, that there could be at least a discussion on the composition, where you say on the one hand side that the Crisis Staff would also have representatives of political organisations and that you do not know why the SDA was not represented in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously it is possible -- I mean, that that should have been the case, but I don't know. There were very few officials who were in top positions from the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just testing your evidence that this Crisis Staff was in accordance with the existing legislation and regulations. And from your last answer, I take it that you do agree that there could be some discussion about the legality of the composition of your Crisis Staff, but that it's -- wasn't something you had given thought or at least that your thought was the responsibility of others and not of you even though you are presiding over that Crisis Staff for a certain period of time. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is what I can say: That I know who became part of the Crisis Staff. No one from the SDA held office, I mean the kind of office that meant they would be members of the Crisis Staff. That's why they did not become members of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: BUT they were -- SDA was a political organisation and had representatives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a matter for political agreement between the Party of Democratic Action and the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said -- just to follow-up on a little bit of your last answer, you said: "No one from the SDA held office, I mean the kind of office that meant they would be members of the Crisis Staff." That's your evidence; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The kind of office that would make a person a member of the Crisis Staff included the office of President of the Municipal Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, who ex officio was supposed to be president of the Crisis Staff, but was not in this case. Then the president of the Executive Board, the secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence, the secretary for the Secretariat of Economic Affairs, the secretary of the Secretariat for Urban Planning. Then Members of Parliament in the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, then the Territorial Defence Staff president, then the commander of the brigade or battalion, depending on the unit involved in the territory. So then two representatives from the economy, the economic sector, they were members of the Crisis Staff, and also the commander of civilian protection. All of these positions were held by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I'd just point the Chamber to the similarity of the positions that he's mentioned with the list provided here in paragraph 3, and that would complete my questions about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, in paragraph 12 of your statement you say that: "At the outset, people in the territory were organising themselves militarily." So I'm going to take this step by step and first I have a very focused question. When you say "the territory," you mean Pale municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the municipality of Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And were you involved with organising those units?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the units had already been organised in a way. These are units of the people's defence and of the municipal staffs of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I think you added a word which I can't find in the statement. I only read that specific sentence, the second one in paragraph 12 -- no, it's part of the first one. "I can say that at the very outset people in the territory were organising themselves ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. The next sentence refers to TO units, but I should have been clearer that I was using the word "militarily" to describe the next sentence and not that it appeared in the statement. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to look at a couple of documents now in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P3030, page 6 in the English and 7 in the B/C/S. This is a document sent to the command of the SFRY armed forces from the command of the 2nd Military District on the 20th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you see, sir, on that page in the B/C/S point 5: "Volunteer forces in the 2nd VO zone"?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to say to this. This is a document of Commander Kukanjac. What have I got to do with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All I've asked for the moment, sir, is if you see the text I mentioned. Do you see that text?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, I see it, of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 8 in the B/C/S and looking at sub-point (f), it notes that: "The JNA has distributed 51.900 weapons (75%), and the SDS 17.298." Were you aware that the JNA and SDS had distributed tens of thousands of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not. I did not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that amounts between them to the distribution of 69.198 arms; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, if you want me to read out the number that is here I can, but don't make me talk about something that -- that has nothing to do with me, some information that has nothing to do with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 11 in the English and 16 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a list of municipalities and numbers of men, and at point 7 we see: "Pale 2.000." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, what you mean. List of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, we see one column that says "opstina," that's "municipalities"; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the next column refers to men; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it says "men" and I see it says "2.000." I don't know what it means. I don't know what this table means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing has been asked to you up till this moment apart from whether you see in this document the same as Mr. Traldi puts to you. He'll certainly put a question to you in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Directing your attention now below the number 75 where it says: "Total: 69.198." Do you see that as well?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's the same as the number of arms reflected in the text I read you a moment ago; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Number of men, not arms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I mean, that's what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I imagine my math can be checked later, sir, but I would submit that it's the same number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'd ask you, were you aware that 2.000 Serbs in Pale had been armed by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning now to 65 ter 10691. I'm going to ask for page 8 in the English and page 10 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the discussion of Pale begins towards the bottom of the page and in the English it starts where it says: "A number of people wearing camouflage uniforms ..." I want to call your attention to some specific points in that paragraph. First, it says a few sentences later that: "... about 300 armed people from this territory were accommodated on the premises of the Fire Department in Pale. They were in readiness and according to another person, one group had returned that morning from 'sabotage training' in the JNA barracks in Kalinovik that lasted about 20 days ..." You weren't aware of that sabotage training, were you?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not, I was not. This is the first time I see this, what you've just read out to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And turning to the next page in B/C/S, we see language: "Apart from the above, on 01.03 and 02.03 a large number of Serbs received weapons at the V.P. Koran and the weapons from the TO staff warehouse were distributed by Radoja Vojvodic, teacher at a primary school and reserve officer in," at the very end continues to the next page in English, at the top, "reserve officer in the JNA ..." Were you aware that JNA officers were involved in distributing arms to Serbs in Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that. Believe me, I just know that the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence had a certain quantity of weapons and they had it under their control. Now, when they distributed that, probably at the very beginning of the war; as for all the rest, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will -- sorry, I would object to inclusion of this document into our case. There is no source because it's not signed, there is no name who produced the document, there is no signature, there is no stamp. This is not a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's a document, but you doubt whether it's an authentic document that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it is not a document. There is no trace who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, every piece --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Every piece of paper with text on it is a document, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you think it has no probative value and it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll ask Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- learn from Mr. Traldi who made this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, where does it come from? Who is the author? Who produced it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My information indicates it was received from the RS on 27 November 2002 and has been admitted in the Krajisnik case. I'm happy to have it MFI'd and provide further information after the break if that's helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, objections against it being MFI'd at this moment so that Mr. Traldi could provide further information?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't like when something is MFI'd because later on it always becomes an evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not true, Mr. Lukic. It sometimes does if there is a satisfactory resolution of the problem that caused it to be MFI'd rather than to be admitted. If that is what you wanted to say, we agree; but it's not what you said. You said MFI-ing --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I agree with what you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it will be MFI'd. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10691 receives number P6565, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. One of the purposes, Mr. Lukic, is also to secure that the document is in the system and cannot be changed again and that we know for sure what document was read by Mr. Traldi. That's one of the purposes for marking for identification, and I think there's every reason to use that instrument to avoid conclusion. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just one more document on this point, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 28476.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Looking at the beginning of the document, it reads: "'At the beginning of September, unknown people started coming to the office of Captain 1st Class Momir Tomcic, they mostly carried bags with SDS emblems ...'" And then it gives some names. And the last sentence of that paragraph reads: "It was agreed at the beginning that under the guise of volunteerism SDS units were to be trained for what is being done now. "In the following days, groups of 15 to 20 men started arriving, first from Sarajevo, then from Pale, Foca, Sokolac ..." And it mentions some other places and it describes the training they received. My question is only: Were you aware that JNA officers were involved in training Serbs from Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know what the month is. September. At that time in 1992 I was not in power. If it's the beginning of September 1991, I wasn't in power then either so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document as well as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection, no stamp, no signature, no number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that, too, I would offer to address at the beginning of the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the document will be MFI'd. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28476 receives number P6566, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, the witness said "if this happened in September ..." of course the document dates back to May 1992, at least that's what we find as a date on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to conclude this topic. The Chamber has also received evidence - and I'd refer to P2001, page 73 in the English and 97 in the B/C/S - that Momcilo Mandic told the RS Assembly that together with Stanisic he "pulled out 560 Hecklers from the MUP to Romanija and distributed them to Sokolac, Rogatica, Han Pijesak, and Pale." Now, my first focused question for you: Mr. Mandic and Mr. Stanisic were both officials in the Bosnian Serb Ministry of the Interior; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They were in the leadership, I mean the Ministry of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And were you aware that Bosnian Serb police officials distributed Hecklers in Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. The police was linked up along the vertical line or chain, and I had nothing to do with the police or the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in light of those pieces of evidence, I'd put to you that it wasn't just that people from Pale were organising themselves militarily, they were receiving assistance from the JNA and from the police, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably there were such cases too but I don't know. I'm not aware of any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm about to turn to a new topic and for continuity I'd suggest that we break a minute early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break now. Mr. Cvoro, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. We take a break first. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I do understand that you wanted the Chamber to move very shortly in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll move into private session for only a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Yes, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we're waiting, there is an issue perhaps we could address and that has to do with the following witness. We were contacted yesterday afternoon by Mr. Lukic, who requested that we switch the witness order to RM311 next and then Mr. Andan following that. We indicated that we do not oppose that witness switch. We're obviously always interested in accommodating witness needs and the efficiency of the trial. We do have concerns in that at 8.48 last night after receiving -- after approving that switch, we received a substantial three-page proofing note. And I can address this at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apart from that matter, when was Chamber staff informed about the wish to change the order of witnesses, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As before, when the Prosecution case was going on, we tried to solve the issue with the Prosecution. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And so we were not informed yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that only in the morning, the staff -- the Chamber staff was informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at what time approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to check that. I don't have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because we were informed by Madam Registrar that there was a possible change already for the next witness, and we were rather surprised that -- because we had no idea and we usually prepare for our hearings as well. We leave it for the time. We'll first continue the examination of the witness, but there is an outstanding issue. You do not oppose but ...?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We do not oppose, but we want to place the issue of this late disclosure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- simply on the record, Your Honour, for future reference potentially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is on the record hereby. Thank you, Ms. Bibles. Mr. Traldi. Mr. Cvoro, apologies for having to finalise a few procedural matters that kept us busy in your absence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to turn now to the group of prisoners from Bratunac who were brought to Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For reference, this is discussed in paragraph 16 of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask some simple questions about that group. First, there were about 400 men in the group of prisoners; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately that number. I don't know precisely, but yes, I think that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you personally learned about the prisoners from representatives of the Pale police; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Early in the morning, police representatives woke me up and they said they had a problem regarding these prisoners that were arriving. Men, actually, people, I can't say "prisoners."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was because this fell under the responsibility of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that they fell under the responsibility of the Crisis Staff, but we felt responsible to protect them in some way and provide for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say "we," you are referring to the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes, the Crisis Staff and the police in whose jurisdiction this was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, after you found out, you gathered the Crisis Staff together; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I gathered the Crisis Staff, but I must say that I don't know the reason why, how it came about that they came to Pale. To this day I don't know this. But when we were brought to the wall, when the people came, I was afraid. Immediately I called the Crisis Staff together and I assigned people to go and talk to Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, and the prime minister. They went and they talked to them. We lodged a protest about why those people had come to Pale. Mr. Karadzic reacted very quickly and positively. He said -- I'm not sure whether he was there at that moment or not, but he was consulted. And he said that not a hair from their heads could be harmed, that they had to be sent to the area where they belonged, in the direction of Sarajevo, as quickly as possible --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I think you --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and there was also an order --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think you've slightly exceeded the question that I asked you, and I appreciate that you want us to understand the details. What I'm going to do next is show you two orders, and perhaps if the one you were about to mention is different, we can discuss it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P3177.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order signed by Branko Djeric to the Sokolac Crisis Staff. And directing your attention to point 1, it refers to the transport of prisoners from Pale to Visoko via Ilijas. This group of prisoners was taken towards Ilijas from Pale; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's right, based on what you've just told us, that the republic-level authorities in the RS were involved in organising the transport of this group of prisoners; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct -- or rather, not directly but according to the document, yes, they did take part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not just according to the document, but you testified that Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, and the prime minister were consulted; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 03681. And, Your Honours, for the record, that past document, P3177, is also discussed in P3170, RM85's 92 bis evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this document is addressed to the Ilijas Crisis Staff and reads: "Please approve and provide passage through your territory for the group of prisoners who are presently at Pale and travelling to Visoko ..." It says they were travelling towards Visoko; that was in Muslim territory. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was the Ilijas territory which was controlled by Muslim forces, but here it states: "In the territory of the municipality of Visoko ..." I don't know any details, but I had information that they had gone to the Ilijas municipality area, which was controlled by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it says next: "Transport and escort for those prisoners will be provided by the Crisis Staff Pale." It was, in fact, the Pale police that secured the transport of the prisoners as they were taken onwards; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the police was in charge of security and to ensure that the prisoners went to the entity border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you the following, earlier when you used the word "prisoners," you said: "... the people who were arriving. Men, actually, people, I can't say 'prisoners.'" Now, in your last answer you refer to them as prisoners, as all the documents apparently do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the point of view of Pale, they were not captured; they had simply arrived. No one captured them in Pale, but I see that the terminology that is being used in these documents is "prisoners." As far as we were concerned, it was just arrival on the Pale territory. We did not consider them captured. We did not capture them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you serious in telling us that if someone is not captured at the place where he's transported through, that he certainly is just a person and not a prisoner anymore? If we transfer a prisoner from prison A to prison B and they pass by Vienna, does that mean that in Vienna he is not a prisoner any further because he was not captured in Vienna? Are you seriously telling us that if you don't capture them, that they're just ordinary people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't have any experience with prisoners, but I did have this experience of people coming there. I don't know how it was -- I mean, it's possible that they were being treated as prisoners, but I don't know how they were captured. It's possible that they were captured by the very fact that they had come there. It's possible, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they in a situation where you would say they were fully free to move around as they wished or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I don't know why, because of what reason, how they had arrived. But they were not free to move around normal, of course not, because they were there, they were simply brought in front of the police station. So what were we supposed to do in the Crisis Staff? How to treat them? But we reacted quickly, we intervened, and we did what we thought was best in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you considered them to be in a position in which they were not free to move and in that respect could be considered to be prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then they didn't have freedom of movement, at that time, because of their own security but also the security of all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Security of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was threatened by their arrival, I myself and many other Crisis Staff members. If you have 400 people coming to the territory of ours -- I mean, if you understand me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do not fully understand because there seems to be a suggestion in your answer that they were a threat to you. I now understand from the follow-up --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, they were not. I'm just talking about some kind of moral endangerment simply because of that number of persons who had arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so if you would have to be protected against anything, it would have been against those who brought them there, because I do understand that they did not come voluntarily. So if you needed to be protected, it was not against these men but against those who brought them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, the people who had brought them to the Pale area in that manner, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what had they to be protected against? What was threatening them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From reprisals by people who did not feel the same way in relation to them. There were always extremists who would maybe be responsible for some incidents. Our objective was to avoid all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did they have to be protected in any way against being perhaps detained without a proper cause? Did you consider that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was police protection. The police station in Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not understood me well. Was there any thought that those you saw to be not free to move around should be protected against being deprived of their liberty illegally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Definitely, they should have been protected from that and they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, they were not free to move, if I understand, so they may have been illegally detained at this moment. You considered them -- you saw them in a prison, prisoner-like situation. Have you ever thought about inquiring into whether they were deprived of their liberty in accordance with the law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Evidently they were not deprived of their freedom in accordance with the law. They had been brought in because they -- by the very virtue of the fact that they were brought in, in that situation they were denied their freedom of movement and all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and you have not considered what you could do to restore their freedom of movement so as to go home again and live their lives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would have been very risky, Your Honour. We felt that our priority was to provide food for them, to provide some kind of accommodation - I cannot say whether it was adequate accommodation - and then to safely see them leave for wherever they were going and this is what we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it relevant to know whether they -- if illegally deprived of their liberty, whether they could go home again where they came from or that they were escorted out of the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not decide these things. Other people decided where they would be going, how, and in which way, but we did lodge a protest, a very strenuous protest over their having been brought to Pale in such a way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if I understand you well, mainly because it bothered you, not because it bothered those you considered to be in a position as if they were prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly it bothered them because their lives were at risk by virtue of the fact that they had been brought in such a way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Two brief follow-ups on His Honour's questions, sir. First, you knew these men had been brought to Pale from Bratunac; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out early that morning from the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when Mr. President asked you about them going home, you replied at transcript page 39, line 24: "That would have been very risky ..." So did you know at the time that it would have been dangerous for them to be returned to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we had no means of transporting them. We didn't know where we would be taking them. We addressed the authorities with this question and they made the decision how to do this and they assumed the responsibility for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I want to try again with just a very focused question. You believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, when I listened to your last question, I think it first needs to be explored risky for whom, for the prisoners or for those to intervene. That is an unclear matter at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll start there, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said it would have been risky to return the prisoners home. For whom would it have been risky?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the prisoners, of course. How could we do it freely if there was a war going on all around? If we were to release them suddenly and let them move through that war-affected zone, they could have been killed. How could they move through combat zones? This was the month of May when the situation in Pale was the hardest. The months of May and June were the hardest days for Pale, for the residents and for me as the president. More citizens of Pale got killed during that month of May and June than throughout the rest of the war. And the sentiments of the people were not kind, and I believe that our action was right. We enabled those people to move safely to the territories of the municipalities where they belonged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where did they then belong, could you tell us? How could you tell us where they belonged other than where they came from, their own homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are asking me about things that I did not decide, such as where they would go, in which direction. I was not even able to influence such decisions. What I was able to do as president of the Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stopped you because you expressed that they went where they belonged. I wasn't saying anything about who decided where they belonged, but apparently you considered them to belong not at their own homes but somewhere else. That's what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I misspoke, maybe I didn't express myself very well. They went to places that the authorities had designated, and of course they belonged to the communities where they came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because it's the second time that you used this language, that's why I asked now. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi -- one final question. If you say it was dangerous to bring them back to Bratunac, was that any more dangerous than to bring them from Bratunac to Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how they came. My opinion is that it would have been very difficult to transport them back to Bratunac. That's my opinion, but the decision was not mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but my question was, irrespective of who decided, whether it would have been any more dangerous to take them back to Bratunac than it was then to take them from Bratunac to Pale, that is, in trucks over the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, you mentioned that they were brought to Pale in front of the police station, but the record isn't quite clear who brought them. They were brought there by armed Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how, for what reason or why. All I know is that they were brought and abandoned outside the Pale police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question specifically was whether they were brought there by armed Serbs, not why they were brought there but whether armed Serbs brought them there. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't there when they were brought. I don't know who brought them and who was in the escort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe just one question. Who escorted them to Visoko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were escorted by the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And were the police armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before moving on, Your Honours, I'd tender 65 ter 03681.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03681 receives number P6567, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. It's admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play a video now with 65 ter 22356A. CLSS has pre-confirmed the translation, so my understanding is based on the Chamber's guidance we need only play it once, but of course I stand to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I take it when it has been prepared in such a way that we can look at it once only? May the video be played. No speaking at a volume level that I'm even able to hear. Mr. Stojanovic, if Mr. Mladic wants to consult, you know under what conditions it is permitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that most likely the problem is with CMSS rather than with the Prosecution. Perhaps you move on and that we'll try to give it another try later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'd forgotten that it's IT rather than CMSS. So if I blamed anyone incorrectly, then -- but the emphasis was on that it was not the party that provides the video that is at this moment seen as the cause of the problems. Perhaps you meanwhile move on, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to turn now to the departure of your Muslim neighbours from Pale. I think we agree that the ethnic make-up of Pale changed during the war; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that many Muslims left?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this Chamber has received evidence that one of the reasons Muslims were fearful and wanted to leave Pale was a meeting between Nikola Koljevic and Muslim representatives, where Koljevic said it didn't matter if the Muslims wanted to live with the Serbs because the Serbs didn't want to live with the Muslims. You don't purport to be aware of Mr. Koljevic's position on population transfers, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In your statement you ascribed the departure of Muslims from Pale to their fear of retaliation against them because of some incidents where Serbs were killed in combat; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's certainly one of the reasons. I said a moment ago that the month of May and the month of June were the hardest months for the citizens of Pale. When I say "the citizens of Pale," I mean all of them. It was also the hardest month for the government of Pale and for me as the president of the Executive Board. It was very hard to look in the eye mothers who had lost in just a few days 46 sons, to look in the eyes children who had lost their parents. And I was overcome by fear. How could we after all of that keep the Muslims in Pale?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you just some very specific questions about those incidents. First, you weren't present at any of those combat incidents, were you?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not, but I attended funerals over the course of two days outside the church in Pale. Those were burials of soldiers who were savagely killed outside Zepa. And there was an attack on the stronghold at Trebevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and 12 fighting men of Republika Srpska were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- I will get to each of those. For now, I'm going to ask you first: Can you confirm that you heard about these incidents from others, in whatever manner?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I heard about it from others. I was not a direct participant in those incidents and skirmishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'm going to ask you briefly what you heard as to the date of each incident and I'm going to go one by one. Can we agree to proceed in that manner?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first incident occurred at Renovica --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I will just ask you the date of each incident, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that Renovica incident is the first you list in paragraph 10 of your statement. That occurred on or about the 22nd of May, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the next incident you mention, the killing of JNA soldiers in Dobrovoljacka Street, you heard that was on or about the 3rd of May, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the incident you were mentioning relating to the killing of soldiers from Pale on the way to Zlovrh, that was on or about the 4th of June, correct, also 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that incident happened generally in the Zepa area?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the next incident which you were describing a moment ago as well, the death of 12 soldiers on the front line at Trebevic on the day of the funeral of those soldiers, that funeral obviously took place after the 4th of June; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the last incident you mentioned in your statement related to Serbs in the Pofalici neighbourhood of Sarajevo and you heard that took place in the middle of May 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The expulsion of Serbs from Pofalici; correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you mention a decision that non-Serbs did not have to move out of Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For the record, that's D493, that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That was issued on the 11th of April, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Right at the beginning, the Muslims demanded to be moved out of Pale. It was on the 9th of April. We responded and you have that document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd like to look at the request they sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 30714.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see in the top left it's sent to the Crisis Staff. So going step by step, we see: "Subject: Proposal of Muslim citizens of the Pale and Koran local communes aimed at dealing with the newly created situation concerning the arrests of unarmed members of the Muslim community." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's it. I can see it now. I'm reading. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And looking at the first paragraph, it refers to the date 9 April 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 9 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I want to just look at a couple of points in this document. Looking first at point 4, it notes -- it requests: "That representatives of the Muslims and other citizens be co-opted into the Pale municipal Crisis Staff." Now, you testified earlier today that everyone on the Pale municipal Crisis Staff was a Serb. Can we take it this request was not accepted?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I responded in my document that all these relations between the SDA and the Serbian Democratic Party, that everything was decided between those two parties. So they were not co-opted by the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So just taking it step by step, no Muslims became members of the Crisis Staff, did they?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the position you occupied, whether you would become a member. No Muslim occupied such a position that would make him eligible for becoming a member of the Crisis Staff. I've already described this. It doesn't mean that there should have been no Muslims on the Crisis Staff. Perhaps there should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now looking at point 10, here we see that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And point 10 will require us, I think, to go to the next page in B/C/S. And if we can zoom in on the bottom of the page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it reads: "That persons and families who do not feel safe on the territory of Pale municipality be allowed to leave the area without hindrance and in an organised manner." That's the request; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then it continues - we'll need to turn to the next page in English - with an explanation: "(Due to reasons such as abuse, unlawful arrests of only Muslims, break-ins into apartments, disarming Muslim police officers, seizing personal weapons with permits and similar)." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've read this correctly, but it doesn't necessarily mean that things were the way it's stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, first I'll tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30714 receives number P6568, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6568 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence of a number of the things described in that paragraph in Exhibit P260. For brevity, let's just look at disarming Muslim police officers, and if we could have 65 ter 30716.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, aren't you going to show my reply, that is to say, the reply of the Crisis Staff to this Muslim request?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Chamber has the benefit of your reply, D493, and it was discussed on direct examination. Now, this article, which we can zoom in towards the top left of the B/C/S version, is titled: "Pursuant to the Order of the 'Government of the Romanija SAO.'" And it explains as it says in the title: "Why Muslim and Croatian policemen were removed from the Pale and Sokolac SJB's ..." And it's dated 26 March 1992. The Muslim police had been removed from the Pale SJB by then; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that the Serbs from Stari Grad and Centar municipality were first removed in some way from their police stations, and then they came to Pale. This was followed by the removal of Muslims from Pale. Considering that this was in the jurisdiction of the ministry and the police stations, I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I can just summarise your answer or perhaps point to some salient features of it. I think you agreed that the Muslim police from Pale were removed; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the expulsion, or rather, removal of Serbs from the Stari Grad and Centar municipalities, Muslims were removed from the Pale police station. I personally received in my office those people who had come from Sarajevo, looking for a way to connect their years of service, their years of pensionable service. I suppose they resolved that problem eventually. Those were active-duty policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30716 receives number P6569, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'll show you one more document before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P262.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be an order you signed on the 7th of May, 1992. Now, this order relates to disconnecting certain phone numbers. I'm not going to ask you about the telephone system, but I'll ask you some specific questions about this document. In paragraph 13 of your signed statement for the Karadzic case, you said: "It is an order to switch off the phone numbers of 15 persons of Muslim nationality according to the Law on Territorial Defence at that time, private resources necessary for the functioning of the authorities could be employed. As far as I recall, it was about people who had already left the territory of Pale municipality and their apartments or houses." So I'll ask you a couple of focused questions about that evidence. Do you confirm today that this order refers to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, let me tell you one thing. You said I signed it? In fact, I didn't. This is not our stamp. As far as I can see, this is the Serbian Democratic Party, but I can give you an explanation, as I did before when testifying in the Karadzic case --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For the moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please first answer the question. You'll have an opportunity to further explain after you've answered the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll ask again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.
