utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you confirm today that this order refers to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you can see that from the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that your recollection is these Muslims had left Pale before 7 May when you signed the order?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, I did not sign this, as you pretend, but it's evident -- or, rather, I suppose that they had by that time already left Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, perhaps it helps you that in the English version of this document it reads at the end, above the signature: "In the place of the president of the Crisis Staff of the Pale municipality, Zdravko Cvoro ..." and then between brackets it reads: Signed by someone else. So there seems to be no --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We may have to go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second page of the English version. Mr. Traldi, this is just one of those examples where a proper introduction of the document, that is, date, author, signature, et cetera, especially if it raises any issues, that the way to do it is: This is a decision, et cetera, it is signed, as the document says, on your behalf but not by you, so that we can avoid these kind of discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course you're correct, Mr. President. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think we might be at the time for the break, Your Honour, and I am about to turn to a slightly different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have no further questions on this document and no follow-up on --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No follow-up on this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we take a break, but could I first ask that Mr. Cvoro would be escorted out of the courtroom. My information, Mr. Traldi, by the way, is that after the break the video system would be functional again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I appreciate that information being provided, Mr. President, and we'll certainly be turning to a different topic then after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We take a break and we'll resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Traldi, perhaps while we are waiting for the witness to come in, with these phone numbers, you said these are Muslim numbers, the witness says but they had left already, is it the position of the Prosecution that they had not left yet? Or is it the position of the Prosecution that they -- it's despite the fact that they may have left and that these may have been empty houses, it nevertheless is discriminatory on ethnic grounds?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's the Prosecution's position, first, other evidence, such as P260, indicates a larger number of Muslim phone numbers were disconnected.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, the fact that they had left already at that stage is relevant to evaluating the reasons that Muslims were leaving Pale municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not challenged, that part of the answer of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you may proceed. We had a little technical delay, Mr. Cvoro, so that explains our late start. Mr. Traldi will now continue. And I think you will play the video if I am looking at my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You have anticipated me correctly, Mr. President. I'm going to ask again that we play a video with 65 ter 22356, and I understood the last time we discussed it that we'll only have to play it once. 22356A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Two and a half thousand men, exclusively from the municipality of Bratunac near the Drina, survived a real massacre after they trudged through the wilderness without clothes or shoes on for eight days before they reached Visoko, where they were provided with accommodation in the sports hall and medical help in the health centre. Many of them made their last steps on that way. Witnesses are talking about hundreds of killed at their house doors and at the local stadium in Bratunac where they were brought to by Seselj's and Arkan's people assisted by the local Serb population. The ones that were not shot were tortured and beaten almost to death. "How many days did you spend in Pale? "Three days. "Where are you from? "I'm originally from Prigrad but I lived in Bratunac. And my brother, baker, was working for them. They did not let him go. The last day they surrounded the building and tied him up. I stopped by to buy some bread. They left my brother ... they beat, beat, beat him the whole day ... and he says ... he says ... look, your brother is killed and tomorrow it will be you. "You can see it well here. I was beaten all over my back. "This here, this is the cross made by a knife; is that right? "Yes, by a blunt knife. "Blunt knife? "What did they beat you with? "They beat me with iron sticks. They beat me with everything, other things, wooden. "Were you beaten in Bratunac or Pale? "In Bratunac, this was in Bratunac. "Both in Bratunac and Pale. "This was in Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You can see that the men from Bratunac had been abused before they arrived in Pale, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You can see on the video the injuries from the beatings, can't you?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see the video, but I don't know if this is authentic. I mean, I cannot say anything, I cannot confirm this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for my understanding, you leave it open that this was staged, that these woundings on the back or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, believe me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you don't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about it. I don't have any knowledge of this having happened in Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Traldi said that it happened before - that's, I think, the question. "You can see that the men from Bratunac had been abused before they arrived in Pale, hadn't they?" So if you say, "I don't know anything about what happened in Pale," Mr. Traldi is putting it to you whether you agree with him that they had been abused before they arrived in Pale.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's possible that they had been abused. From this footage we can see that they had been abused, but whether that was in Bratunac or somewhere else, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. The question was not whether it happened in Bratunac. The question was about whether it happened before they arrived in Pale, wherever that may have been. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video receives number P6570, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6570 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to put a question to the witness in this context. When these -- when the prisoners arrived in buses in Pale, did you meet them personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not meet them when they arrived. Is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. That was what I'm -- was asking --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not present when they arrived. I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that -- yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I was just asking you if you saw them. Did you see them later when they stayed in Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, I did not see them. I did not see them when they left either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means that you never have seen this group of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now to a different topic. At the beginning of the war there were three mosques in Pale municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Pale specifically, the town, there was not a single mosque, but in the municipality of Pale there were three mosques.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Those mosques were preserved as long as the Muslim population was present; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And all of them were destroyed after that, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was not in power when they were destroyed. While I was in power, they were intact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why are you again and again -- you are not under attack here. You appear as a witness to tell us what you know. You're not here to respond to blame -- being blamed for what happened when you were in power. You're here to answer questions. Now, the question simply was whether the mosques were intact as long as the Muslims were there and that they were destroyed after that, irrespective of who's responsible, who did it, whatever, just a matter of fact. Could you please answer the question as it was put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Judge. After the Muslims left, as far as I know, the mosques were destroyed. How and in which way, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one asked you. They were destroyed therefore. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have, turning now to the convoys out of Pale, if we could have Exhibit P3972.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see that these are minutes of the Pale Municipal Assembly on 18 June 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 4 in both languages, the bottom of the page in English and the middle of the page in B/C/S, at item 2 refers to a discussion and the opinions of the Assemblymen on the issues of Muslims moving out of the territory. Several lines below that it reads: "The President of the Assembly and the Chairman of the Executive Committee ..." Now, the chairman of the Executive Committee would be you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "... objected to the activities of the public security station in this respect because it had" - and now we need to turn to the next page in English - "participated in the attempt to organise the Muslims and move them out, which had been done without a political decision which meant that the official structures of power had been bypassed. This was why the attempt had been prevented." So the police had been involved in pressuring Muslims to leave Pale even before this meeting on the 18th of June; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this statement -- well, I agree with this statement but these were exceptional cases. I mean, generally -- well, it was individuals probably who abused their positions and that is why we lodged this protest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, after this decision was issued - I'm not asking now about the content of the decision but about how it was perceived - after the decision was issued, Muslims interpreted it as saying that they had to move out of Pale municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- well, that's why I said that. Many people abused and misinterpreted the decision, but this kind of decision -- well, it didn't say that they must, et cetera, it is the way it's been written.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And people abusing and misinterpreting the decision included Serbs who applied pressure on Muslims to leave; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. There were individuals who interpreted this in their own way and exerted pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm done with this document. If we could have P264. This is a decision of the Pale SJB issued on the 2nd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this decision grants the request by Muslim and Croatian citizens living in the Pale centre to move out; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the public security station was in charge and in the Assembly decision -- I mean - how do I put this? - there was this conclusion to do it this way and probably they did it on the basis of the decision of the Assembly of the municipality of Pale, as written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at the end it says: "We hereby call on police and military patrols to enable the unobstructed passage of three buses transporting Muslim civilians in their respective territories." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you read it correctly, as it is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So it's right that Muslim civilians were transported out of Pale by police officers of the Pale SJB; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims on the basis of their requests and the lists that were kept by the centre of public security, escorted by the police, left in an organised fashion in the direction of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And they were transported towards Stari Grad, Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, all of that is Sarajevo. Pale used to be a Sarajevo municipality too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the old area of Sarajevo, that would have been on the other side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was the Serb municipality of Stari Grad and the federal Muslim municipality of Stari Grad, the old town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the federal municipality would have been in Muslim territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And on the other side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: These people's transport out of Pale was covered in the media; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I'm not sure. I haven't read this. At that time there was only the SRNA news agency, there was the radio, there was TV Republika Srpska with its headquarters in Pale. They probably followed all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, if we could have 65 ter 30717.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put first a question with respect --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- to the document on the screen. Mr. Cvoro, this decision is called: "Decision to grant the request made by citizens of Muslim and Croatian citizens living in the Pale centre." Do you know if all citizens of Muslim and Croatian ethnicity signed such a request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think it was the obligation of the Assembly, that -- that people move out voluntarily. Now, I don't know whether everybody signed that or not, but I think that most of them did sign this request to leave because that was the decision of the Assembly too. This is a constitutional right of each and every citizen guaranteed by the constitution, that they can live wherever they want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And if a Muslim or a Croat would have preferred to stay, what would happen to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he'd enjoy all the civic rights enjoyed by other citizens of Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you know of any such a case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Above the place where I lived, there was this lady who was in this weekend cottage all along and she died of old age. She walked around, did her own shopping, et cetera. Her first name was Zerina, I don't know her last name. There are other such cases too, but I don't know individually. I know of this specific case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And she stayed after the moving out of the other Muslim and Croatian citizens; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. She stayed. After Dayton they made an offer to her, asking whether she wanted to leave. They were also looking for her from Zenica and she said: No, I want to stay here with the people who accepted me like a normal citizen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I contacted her --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- a countless number of times and I asked her if she had any problems and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You answered my question. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To follow up on His Honour's question, this is labelled a request made by citizens of Muslim and Croatian citizens, so one of the requests -- one of the rights that large numbers of Muslim and Croatian citizens don't seem to have enjoyed is the right to stay free of the fear that you describe in your statement that you say made them want to leave; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, it is only human to be frightened, to be afraid. There's not a single person who is not afraid. I was frightened too and I left. So why force someone to stay on if they wish to leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You left Sarajevo, correct, and went to Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with my family, with my children who were underage. When I decided -- when I was trying to make a decision as to whether I should leave or not, I thought it's better for me to make a decision and leave than to repent all my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 30717.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an article from Oslobodjenje on the 3rd of July. I had asked a minute ago if this was covered in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on the bottom of the page centre in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this refers to the people who'd been expelled from Pale; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the media from Sarajevo as far as I can see. Croats -- many Croats -- actually, I didn't say that. Many Croats did not leave, they stayed on in Pale. Obviously this is the right of each and every journalist, writer, to write whatever they deem fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd asked a simple question which was: This refers to the people who'd been expelled from Pale; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that people were not expelled from Pale. They left upon their own request.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's drop that term, then, for a moment. This refers to people who had left Pale; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be put that way too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30717 receives number P6571, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Perhaps, Mr. Traldi, it's -- before we continue. Witness, is it clear what happens at this moment during the examination? Is it clear to you? And perhaps I take one example to just explain to you. In your statement at paragraph 10, you list a long series of incidents where Serb people were wounded or killed, and then in that same paragraph you say: Well, the Muslim population of Pale will have left because they feared retaliation and they felt unsafe since those crimes had been committed by their Muslim compatriots. That's your explanation, and you said they requested to leave. Now, Mr. Traldi puts all these incidents to you and makes clear that all these incidents happened after the discussion on a decision on whether Muslims would leave or would not leave. That's one. Second, he puts to you this request which doesn't say: We fear retaliation, but we are abused, we are arrested, we are whatever. What Mr. Traldi is doing, he puts to you that your undocumented and to the extent it is documented, that is, referring to specific incidents, just can't be true because these incidents happened after they requested to leave; and second, in their request they clearly state that it's because of the abuse that they want to leave and not out of fear of retaliation. Now, this happens during the whole of this examination. Do you have -- first of all, I would like to know for certain that you understand what Mr. Traldi is doing, that Mr. Traldi makes an effort to demonstrate that what you said is inconsistent with the timing of the incidents you rely on; and second, that it is inconsistent with the reasons given in this document. I want you to be sure that you understand what now happens in this cross-examination so that you have a fair opportunity to respond to what Mr. Traldi did not specifically mention to be inconsistent, but he clearly suggests that your statement is inconsistent with both the timing of the incidents and inconsistent with the documentary evidence related to the expressed wish of Muslims, why they want to leave. I think it would be fair that you have an opportunity - and I just give this as one of the examples of many - that you comment on what seems to be the core issue of the cross-examination, but therefore I wanted you to be aware of what it exactly is. And perhaps you could use this example which I gave about the inconsistencies, to say something about it, not about all kind of other things but about the inconsistencies which are clearly at the centre of the cross-examination. If you want to say something about it after I've explained to you what the issue is, then of course you're free to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge, sir. All of these things that happened, of course, influenced the decision that was reached and the fear of the Muslims, why they wanted to leave Pale. We've discussed that, what were the things that happened that made the Muslims consider leaving Pale. Since this is very important -- a very important question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to understand you correctly. I pointed at two things: First, inconsistency in chronology with the incidents; and the second, the reasons given by the Muslims in that document why they wanted to leave. Now, you started your answer by saying: "All of these things that happened ..." What are you referring to? Are you talking about the incidents which came --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mentioned events about which the Prosecutor -- the gentleman of the Prosecution asked me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That he says came after the request in which the Muslims said: We are abused, we want to leave. So that could not -- that's clearly the position of the Prosecution, that could not have explained fear for retaliation for events that had not yet happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've said that there were individual pressures from the police and from some other people to have the Muslims leave. Misinterpretation of the decision - I've already said that - all of these things, of course, influenced people and raised their concerns and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the written request was before the decision, but let me just remember the chronology. The request in which the Muslims said, the last portion, we'd like to leave, that was late March?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The 9th of April --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 9th of April --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and the decision was taken on the?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: On the 11th of April they issued a decision saying the Muslims didn't have to leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- and then on the 18th of June a decision saying they could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, Witness, if the witness -- if the Muslims requesting to be able to leave, if they rely on abuse, arrest, et cetera, that -- if that is preceding the decision, then a misinterpretation of the decision could not have caused them to write that down because they wrote it down before the decision was there. So I'm just trying to understand your logic, your reasoning, and I find that you often give explanations which are contradicted by at least documentary evidence that is put before us, whether true or not but -- so if you say all this happened, you say individual abuse, that could not explain what the witness expressed as their fear, that is, that they were arrested, they were abused, et cetera, because the decision -- a misinterpretation of the decision, the decision wasn't there yet. Therefore, I give you an opportunity to come with precise explanations which are in line with what we heard from other sources. I interrupted you because you said -- you started your answer by saying: "All of these things that happened, of course, influenced the decision that was reached and the fear of the Muslims, why they wanted to leave Pale ..." That is still not an answer to the two inconsistencies I mentioned to you. Muslims saying we -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I speak? I think - I don't know if I understood you correctly - but at the very beginning, on the 9th of April, the Muslims stated their requests to leave and they gave their reasons for doing so. There was a response from the Crisis Staff to this document and we believed - I believed - that this was in some way a completion of that first part. Later, life, work went on in Pale. Then a series of events ensued in Pale which happened from that time until the time when the decision was reached. And I explained that as well. And I said that after all of these problems that cropped up, that I talked about, on which I was questioned by the Prosecutor, what followed was a debate in the Assembly regarding renewed requests by Muslims individually and collectively to leave Pale. The decision was reached. After the decision of the 19th, I think it was, the Muslims began to move out. They had time to think about it, to look at the situation in depth, and then only in July they began to move out. They were leaving in an organised manner with their own private vehicles, with all of the things that they could carry with them. And I don't know what else I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then two short questions. Is it true that in your statement I do not find anything about Muslims requesting to be able to leave because they were abused, illegally arrested, et cetera, that although the document says so, that you have not mentioned that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't -- I didn't have that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the other document not shown to you in another case, the request, the request -- the long request, last final paragraph, you never seen that before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw the first request of the 9th of April. I don't know whether that request -- I think -- I think that we resolved a lot of things as we went along and we responded to that request by a document that's there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you about whether I found those reasons: Abuse, being arrested and other things, the reasons why they wanted to leave, whether we find anything about that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. That was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the only question that remained. Mr. Traldi -- my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I do still have a few more, Your Honour. If we could have P3800.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, you've just said that the Muslims moved out with their own private vehicles. So what I'm showing you is a report from the Pale SJB dated 6 July 1992, and it describes this series of convoys. And looking at the second paragraph first, it says: "On 30 June 1992, 88 Muslim citizens (women, children, and men) were transferred in two buses, escorted by police officers of the Pale SJB ..." And then it describes the route. The paragraph below it says: "On 1 July 1992, 220 citizens were transferred in four buses, on 1 July 1992, 324 citizens in five buses, and on 3 July 1992, 410 citizens in seven buses, totalling 1.042 citizens." So the Pale SJB reported that it had conducted this transfer by bus, not in the Muslims' private vehicles; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, no, but there were cases where there were also cars along with the buses.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to repeat the last sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think the interpreters didn't hear the last sentence of your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally not -- they couldn't take each and every private vehicle with them, and it's a question whether all of them had their own cars. But I know that along with some -- with the buses, there were some private vehicles that went in the direction of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'll just have three more documents for you, one more on this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 03730. And could we first turn to the second page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As whose signature do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning back to the first page, this is a document sent from the Pale Executive Committee to the Wartime Board of Commissioners, personally to Ms. Plavsic. Now, she was a member of the War Commission; right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was a commissioner of the Pale municipality on behalf of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in fact we see - it's now on page 2 in the B/C/S but at the bottom of the page 1 in the English - that this was copied to the Presidency of the RS government; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I apologise to the usher, but if we could go back to page 1 again. In the second paragraph, this refers to the decision from the 18th of June, and then it notes: "Muslims started moving out forcefully and wilfully at their own private initiative and discretion and with their own subjective interpretation of the decision ..." That's right, isn't it, that other Muslims had fled Pale before the convoys that we were just discussing?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 03730.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03730 receives number P6572, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to conclude by very briefly discussing your evidence about the Muslim municipality you say was established. That included the Renovica area; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your evidence is that area was never taken over by the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the entire territory, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Some parts, however, were; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because there was a barracks in Renovica. The soldiers were guarding these barracks until the time that they got all the assets, the equipment, out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 30712. This is an SRK report from the 14th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And directing your attention to point 2, I'm just going to read the first sentence: "Our units in Renovica area continued an offensive and liberated Renovica ..." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did read it out, but I don't have information about the whole of Renovica, that entire area ever being completely liberated. It's possible that this is discussing the actual settlement of Renovica, but there are also other settled places, villages, in the Renovica area and a part also is related to Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You'd agree with me, though, I expect, that this does not simply speak of guarding a barracks but of liberating an area; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims attacked police forces right at the beginning and killed two policemen and wounded five of them. Then in that area there was a conflict, fighting went on, certain lines were established where fighting was going on in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30712 receives number P6573, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6573 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And finally, if we could have 65 ter 09822. This is a document emanating from SJB Visegrad and it's dated the 30th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, initially it refers to a number of locations. I'd just direct your attention to the second point, it's a number of locations including Renovica; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the 30th of July, 1995. I wasn't even close to these events and the situation. I don't even know why you're asking me about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No question is yet put to you, Witness, so don't worry. Wait for the question. And if you don't know anything about what Mr. Traldi asks you, then you just tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you do see the mention of Renovica in the second point; correct? Zlovrh, Podzeplje, Dzimrije, Sokolovici, Stijenice, Renovica? And I apologise to the witness for my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes. It's mentioned, it's written down, but I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It does read below that: "All directions are mainly unpopulated and before the war they were populated by Muslim inhabitants." Do you see that language?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 09822 receives number P6574, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6574 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that completes my examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. We had a late start after the break. Mr. Lukic, could you tell us how much time you would need, approximately, if you have any further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you at this moment, really. I was trying to calculate, but I don't think I will finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then perhaps it would be better to take the break first so that you are better able to organise yourself and that the next witness is informed that his appearance today is not to be expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, if it's only for two or three minutes, then of course it doesn't make sense to let him wait for that. Let's take the break first and let's see how matters develop. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whilst we are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, Mr. Lukic, for the next witness if you would need tomorrow another five or seven minutes, we have to take a break after that because the next witness would require some preparations, technical preparations, in terms of protective measures. I'm not -- I'm just -- I leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll see after today's day how much I -- maybe I would know better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, you'll now be further examined by Mr. Lukic. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day once again, Mr. Cvoro.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We haven't seen each other for a long time, so just refer to me as sir, attorney, but I am attorney Branko Lukic. You were shown a lot of documents today.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I understand that perhaps this has created confusion with the Trial Chamber as well as to what came before what, so I'm going to go through it and recapitulate, look at the times -- timing to see whether what you are saying makes sense and whether it's contrary to what the documents show. I want to begin a few days before the request of the 9th of April, 1992. Do you remember that on the 6th of April, 1992, Bosnia and Herzegovina broke away from the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think the question is leading in its form.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is re-direct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. At the same time, is there any dispute about it? It's an -- seems to be an introduction to what then follows. If you really want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think that it would be inappropriate to lead the witness on the 6th of April as Bosnia and Herzegovina separating from the Socialist Federal Republic, then please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, I suppose on that issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three days after Bosnia and Herzegovina broke away from Yugoslavia, on the 9th of April, 1992, thus comes this request for Muslims to move out from the territory of the municipality of Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's when the request came. I think it was very soon after the decision to secede.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of April, two days after this request, a decision was adopted and Muslims were informed that there was no need for them to move out, they didn't have to do that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I signed the decision and I dispatched it to the city address.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of June, 1992, two months and seven days later, a decision was adopted saying that they can move out?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this first: On the 9th of April and the 11th of April, was there any fighting in Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And between these two days, between the 11th of April when the Muslims were told: You don't have to move out, and the 18th of June, when they were told: You can move out if you wish, the following events took place and you listed them and I'm going to list them again. On the 3rd of May, 1992, the JNA was attacked in Dobrovoljacka Street?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In mid-May, the Serbian settlement of Pofalici in Sarajevo was attacked?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that attack --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The list is still clear in our memory, including the dates, unless you disagree with the dates suggested by Mr. Traldi. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After this attack on Pofalici, did the Serbs from Pofalici come to Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs from Pofalici came to Pale, they were expelled. They came with no clothes, in their bare feet. I was woken up by the police in the middle of the night, this was in the middle of the night. They told me that a large number of Serbs from Pofalici had arrived in Pale. I didn't know what to do at that point, so we opened up the elementary school where we put them up and we provided some initial assistance to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 22nd of May, what happened in Renovica?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two policemen were killed and five were wounded while they were disarming the citizens of Renovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then on the 4th of June you told us Zlovrh Zepa, 46 soldiers were killed; you told us that after a few days, when these 46 soldiers were being buried, there was another attack at another position which was then taken up already by the RS soldiers, when 12 soldiers were killed?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the second day of the burials there was a strong attack on Trebevic. Many people from in front of the church went away then and they didn't come back. They went to defend the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A document was forgotten in this recapitulation of the events and I will mention it. I think it's included.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at D495 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So on the 18th of June, the decision was made that Muslims may leave Pale municipality in an organised way, and we see a request here dated 22nd June 1992, where a group departure of Muslims is requested, and the listed families are indicated together with their numbers. So there were more requests, not just one. This is another one dated 22nd June.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that decision was made by the Assembly, many requests started arriving at the public security station and most of the Muslims left for Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did the organised departure of Muslims from Pale begin?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in the end of June and beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another document was shown to you. Just a moment. There are many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter is -- 65 ter 3730 is the number that I have I hope we'll -- no, it's now marked as P6572. We'll have it on the screen soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the document that you signed, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. That's from the War Commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this document dated 7 July 1992, you said: "Contrary to the decision of the Pale Municipal Assembly made at its session of 18 June 1992, which regulated the issue of changing the place of residence of non-Serbian residents, Muslims started moving out in a coerced way and this was done wilfully at some people's own initiative ..." Did you mean by this that somebody expelled them from their homes wilfully or that they left outside of the convoys of their own will?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think anybody drove them out nor did they wilfully leave. They only started interpreting this decision in their own way, as meaning that they had to leave Pale. I'll just give you one example. My own place of residence, in fact, where I was born, was Bogovici, a bit further away, and some Muslims from Bogovici had come to ask me how to understand this decision. They were not very educated people, village people, and they asked: Does it mean we have to go? And I said: No, that's not what it means. However, the very next day I learned that they too had decided to leave Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then you say that other problems occurred as a consequence of these departures. A large number of illegal and criminal actions, the disposal of movable and immovable property, the impossibility of effectively protecting houses and flats that were left unprotected, the impossibility of taking care after -- taking care of the cattle left behind by previous owners.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all these problems really occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I ask one clarification. This report states that Muslims started moving out in a coerced way. What do you mean exactly by that? Or as it says in the written English translation, started moving out forcefully, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that we have translation issue here. I haven't noticed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could be, but I see that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My proposition is that the witness reads the whole paragraph in B/C/S so it's translated, not reading the text from this translation, but translated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, also we have two, we have the interpreters and we have the translation. As we all know, the interpreters are not supposed to resolve any linguistic issues, but we'll certainly have time until tomorrow to have this portion verified as far as translation is concerned. But if the witness would just read the language in his own and tell us what he meant by that, because I was also puzzled by one of the answers after that which was: I think no one -- let me literally find it. "No one forced them, but also they did not leave wilfully," that's ... Could you please tell us exactly what the document says as far as the Muslims leaving? Read it in your own language and explain it to us and we will meanwhile verify -- yes, the second sentence of the second paragraph we are interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Namely, contrary to the decision of the Municipal Assembly of Pale made at its session of 18 June 1992, which regulated the issue of change of residence of the non-Serb population, by private initiative according to subjective interpretation of the decision and own discretion ..." and then I can't see the remaining text very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If that paragraph, the second paragraph could be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "... there occurred a forced and self-willed evacuation of the Muslim population which opened up a series of other problems such as a large incidence of illegal and criminal actions ..." What I meant here is private decisions of individuals to interpret the decision in their own way, as they wished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm just trying to find -- I see the reference to the session of the 18th of June, also then see which regulated the issue or the question of the changing of the place of residence of the non-Serbian population --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in the middle of the second-last row of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Muslims started moving out --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Odluka" is with a capital and after that it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the "private initiative and discretion," but the part which appears --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Underneath --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly underneath, initiative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, but the part -- "Muslims started moving out forcefully and wilfully" has apparently disappeared entirely now from what the witness -- let me see, that comes then after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Line 11 and 12 of page 83.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters did not repeat the written text because it's wrong, as a translation it's wrong. "Forcefully" means something entirely different than "by force."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I think that we have to review the translation in detail. Perhaps also then we leave it until tomorrow until we have received a new -- the new translation or the verified translation to ask the witness further. There's no need to answer the question at this moment, Mr. Cvoro. The only thing then what remains is: To what extent is leaving on your own contrary to the decision? Why couldn't they leave on their own if they wished to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was self-willed interpretation of this decision both by Serbs and Muslims, and the Muslims interpreted the decision in their own way, whereas other people also exercised coercion, and we, in the institutions, took steps to prevent that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you -- in this document it reads: "Contrary to the decision reached by the Pale SO at its session of the 18th of June ..." And then you explain what happened, including that they on their own initiative started leaving. To what extent is that contrary --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- contrary -- to what extent is that contrary to the decision? Did the decision say: You may not leave at your own initiative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've already said. Some people, let's say Serbs, interpreted the decision as meaning that the Muslims should leave their houses. So they came to these houses and in some way forced the Muslims to leave. On the other hand, Muslims interpreted the decision as meaning that they had to go, which is not what the decision said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. And what, apart from writing personally to Biljana Plavsic, was done to prevent this? Did you immediately issue a clear order that everyone should refrain immediately from compelling Muslims to leave and telling Muslims that the order in no way required them to leave? What did you do in that respect, apart from sending letters which may not have reached the most interested parties, that is, those who forced them out and those who felt that they had to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we reacted. We sent a request to the police to take more serious steps on the ground because it's the police who has to enforce these things, and I gave you one example how I received the Muslims from my own native place, Bogovici, and the explanation I'd given them. I'd explained to them that they didn't have to leave. It was up to them to decide whether they wished to go or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- your testimony gives the impression that there was a widespread misunderstanding of the order. Apart from instructing the police -- first of all, did you instruct the police in writing or just orally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there are later some written documents concerning police actions. I believe there is an order of 16 July related to this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently on the 7th of July the problem has already been noticed. What did you do at that moment? Did you give oral instructions to police or written instructions, I would say, before the 7th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, we sent a report to the commissioner, Biljana Plavsic, and she --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, first of all, my question was: What did you do apart from sending something to Madam Plavsic? And my question simply was, where you told us that you sent a request to the police, whether it was in writing or whether it was oral? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember whether we put anything in writing, but I'm certain we told them verbally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, my next question was: What did you do in a more public way to make sure that everyone would interpret the order correctly, where you had found that many of them had misunderstood it? Did you make a public announcement or did you -- did you do anything in that respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we went to the Muslims and talked to them about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what about the Serbs who had misinterpreted the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's where the police acted quickly and detained some people. I believe they did react.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many people did they detain and do you know who they detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that information. The police have their own line of reporting to the minister and other institutions along their own vertical line. They do it as part of their regular work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if there would be any documentary evidence in that respect that might further strengthen the evidence of the witness, the Chamber would be glad to receive such documentary evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would be glad to find some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can imagine. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document before you on the screen, you are complaining that there is no co-ordination between the police and their work and the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we had no jurisdiction over the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These problems, that it was impossible to look after the housing and the cattle, was that in fact the competence of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another issue listed here is the issue of disposing of the movable and immovable property left behind by previous owners. During your tenure as member of the Executive Board, was there any change of ownership from a Muslim owner to a Serb resident of Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs and the Muslims in Pale knew each other very well. Many of them made contracts between themselves and swapped property in order to protect it. The Serbs gave them the keys to the homes they had left behind in Sarajevo and the Muslims from Pale went to those houses and flats in Sarajevo. The municipality did not have to verify the authenticity of these contracts, but they did verify the signatures on these contracts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the ownership transferred during the war?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I believe there was no transfer of ownership.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was mention of telephone numbers that were switched off and taken over. You had a telephone at your own home?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened with it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me it had to be taken away from me for the needs of the army. I didn't have a telephone at home, and even at the office I had to give up one of the telephone numbers there for the needs of other institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see P6562.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It has been shown to you already today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can break now, but I will have a lot since 15 documents were introduced during the cross-examination. So I will have to open some of them and discuss them with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that's understandable. And that would take you approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Less than first session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Less than first session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try to condense it tonight. When I sit, maybe I can condense my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we might take an early break, then, tomorrow and during the first break have the preparations for the next witness be ready. Mr. Cvoro, we will certainly conclude tomorrow, but not today. Therefore, I instruct you again that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and we would like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.30, in this same courtroom. And we hope that we conclude within approximately one hour. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 5th of June, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of June, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.16 p.m.,
